faq.q: What are the seven ranks of classification?
faq.a: Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species. Each rank is a smaller group inside the one before. A memory aid is King Philip Came Over For Good Soup.
A species is a group of living things that can breed together to produce fertile offspring. Tigers are one species; lions are another.
asks: Tell me about the species level

faq.a: It is the tiger's binomial name, its two-part scientific name. Panthera is the genus and tigris is the species. Scientists everywhere use it, whatever their language.
Carl Linnaeus, a Swedish scientist, set out the system and the two-part naming in the 1700s, especially in his book Systema Naturae of 1758 for animals.

faq.q: Why do scientists classify living things?
faq.a: Classification helps scientists name things clearly, see how they are related, find new species and avoid confusion between local names.

facts: The tiger's scientific name is Panthera tigris; the genus Panthera also includes lions, leopards and jaguars.
Carl Linnaeus popularised two-part (binomial) names in the 1750s.
